title: Access and use information from texts

lessons.title: Workshop texts and how to find information
lessons.html:
Texts in the equipment workshop

A text is any written or visual message. In a farm equipment workshop you read many texts:

  • Operator and workshop manuals
  • Service schedules and checklists
  • Parts catalogues and price lists
  • Labels on oil, grease, coolant and cleaning products
  • Safety signs and warning stickers on machines
  • Job cards and work orders
  • Notices on the notice board

Know what you are looking for

Before you read, decide what you need. For example: 'What is the oil capacity of this gearbox?' or 'Which part number is the fuel filter for this tractor?' Then look only for that.

Finding information fast

  • Contents page: at the front of a manual, it lists chapters and page numbers.
  • Index: at the back, it lists topics in alphabetical order with page numbers.
  • Headings: show what each section is about.
  • Tables: give facts in rows and columns, such as service intervals.
  • Diagrams: show parts with numbers or labels.

Skimming and scanning

Skimming means reading quickly to see what a page is about. Scanning means looking for one fact, such as a torque value or a part number. Run your finger down the page to keep your place.

New words

When you meet a new word, look at the words around it, check the manual's glossary, use a dictionary, or ask the mentor. Write new words in your word book.

Always use the manual for the correct make, model and serial number. Machines that look the same may need different parts or settings.

lessons.title: Reading signs, labels and diagrams
lessons.html:
Information in pictures and symbols

Safety signs

SignMeaning
Red circle with a lineProhibited, do not do this (for example no smoking near fuel)
Blue circleMandatory, you must do this (for example wear eye protection)
Yellow triangleWarning of danger (for example hot surface, electricity)
Green squareSafe condition (first aid, emergency exit)
Red squareFire-fighting equipment

Warning stickers on machines

Tractors and implements carry warning stickers, often with pictures: a hand caught in a belt, a person under a raised implement, or a rotating PTO shaft. These show real dangers. Never remove or paint over them. Report stickers that are damaged or missing.

Product labels

Oil, grease, coolant, battery acid and solvent containers have labels. Look for:

  • Product name and type, such as engine oil grade
  • What it is used for
  • Hazard pictures in red diamonds, for example flammable or corrosive
  • Safety instructions and PPE needed
  • First aid information
  • Storage and disposal instructions

Use the product the manual asks for. The wrong oil can damage an engine or hydraulic system.

Diagrams and exploded views

Parts catalogues use exploded views, drawings where the parts of an assembly are spread out with numbers. Find the number on the drawing, then look up that number in the parts list to get the part number and name.

Gauges and dashboards

Warning lights on a tractor dashboard are a kind of text. Know the symbols for oil pressure, engine temperature, battery charge and hydraulic warning. If a red light comes on, stop the machine safely and check.

lessons.title: Following instructions and using information
lessons.html:
Putting information to work

Following written instructions

  1. Read all the steps first.
  2. Collect the tools, parts and PPE listed.
  3. Follow each step in order. Do not skip steps.
  4. Look at the pictures that go with the steps.
  5. Stop and ask if something is not clear.
  6. Check your work at the end.

Example: reading a service table

ItemEvery 50 hEvery 250 hEvery 500 h
Grease fittingsYesYesYes
Engine oil and filterYesYes
Fuel filtersYes

If a tractor reaches 500 hours, you must grease, change the engine oil and filter, and change the fuel filters. Always use the table in the real manual for that machine.

Facts and opinions

A fact can be checked, such as 'The gearbox takes the oil type listed in the manual'. An opinion is what someone thinks, such as 'Any oil will do'. Follow the facts in the manual, not opinions.

Filling in forms using information

When you fill in a job card, use the information you found: the machine hours from the meter, part numbers from the catalogue, quantities from the manual. Copy numbers carefully and check them twice.

Sharing information

If you read a notice or a service bulletin, tell co-workers who did not see it. Say the main point simply, with important details such as dates or part numbers.

Key points

  • Use the contents page, index, headings and tables to find information quickly.
  • Skim for the main idea; scan for one fact.
  • Learn safety sign colours and never remove warning stickers.
  • Read product labels for use, hazards, PPE and first aid.
  • Use exploded views to find part numbers.
  • Read all steps first and follow the manual for the correct model.
